_readme: Verified source registry for Fact Royale.
A claim verified once is never verified again. Questions cite an entry by id
in sourceRefs rather than carrying a raw URL, so one NASA or Britannica page
can back many unrelated questions, and a source found wrong is fixed once.
FIELDS
tier        primary | reference | secondary
url         canonical link
archive     web.archive.org snapshot. Sources disappear; a citation that
404s in two years is not a citation.
publisher   who is standing behind it
establishes list of specific claims this source proves. One page often
proves several unrelated things; record each separately.
checked     ISO date last confirmed
recheck     ISO date after which to reconfirm. Omit for facts that cannot
change. Saturn's moon count needs one; Hastings does not.
note        caveat, or what should replace this entry
TIERS
primary    the person, institution or document itself. One is enough.
reference  edited reference works. One is enough.
secondary  reporting about a primary source. Needs two, different outlets.
replace     an OPEN action: this entry is not good enough yet and why.
'note' is a permanent caveat; 'replace' is a to-do.
Self-reported first-person accounts where the speaker benefits from the story
are downgraded to secondary and need corroboration. Mark the question
selfReported: true.

Steadicam used for the Overlook corridor shots following Danny; the glides created a new cinematic effect

A 1993 survey found 24% of recruits strongly influenced by TV and films
Taj Mahal begun c.1632 by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal
Mausoleum complete c.1638-39, adjunct buildings 1643, decoration to at least 1647
42-acre complex, roughly 22 years total
UNESCO World Heritage Site 1983
Bell's notebook entry of 10 March 1876 records 'Mr. Watson - Come here - I want to see you'
Bell noted Watson came and confirmed he had heard and understood

No attempt to avoid means no base; the pitch is a strike if in the zone, a ball if not

A pitch that bounces first still awards the base

It displaced Michael Jackson's Dangerous, which had spent four weeks at number one and fell to fifth

recordcollector-nevermind.replace: Single secondary for the 46,251 pressing figure. Find a label or RIAA record.

establishes: Cary Joji Fukunaga won Outstanding Directing for a Drama Series at the 66th Primetime Emmy Awards for True Detective episode 'Who Goes There'
emmy-fukunaga-2014.note: Corroborated by Hollywood Reporter and Variety, 25 August 2014.

establishes: Uros islands are built from totora reed root bundles with dried reed stacked in alternating layers
Islands are anchored to the lakebed with stakes
Lower layers rot and must be continually replaced; a maintained island lasts around thirty years
smithsonian-uros.note: Replaces the Wikipedia entry. The population figure was removed from the question rather than sourced, because no reliable current count exists.

romania-bear-census-2025.publisher: Romanian Ministry of Environment, Waters and Forests
establishes: National genetic census of brown bears, ~24,000 samples across 25 counties, 2021-2025
Final results (December 2025) estimate 10,657 to 12,787 bears on a conservative scenario
April 2025 preliminary figure was 10,419 to 12,770
First scientifically grounded estimate; earlier figures up to 8,000 were observational
romania-bear-census-2025.note: Ministry release is the primary record. Reported independently by AFP/France24 and G4Media. Use the December final figure, not the April preliminary.
romania-bear-census-2025.replace: Link to the December 2025 final report rather than the April preliminary release.

cib-totora-islands.publisher: CIB (International Council for Research and Innovation in Building and Construction)
establishes: Uros island bases are bundled totora roots with dried reed stacked in alternating layers
Islands are anchored with driven stakes; lower layers rot and are replaced from above
cib-totora-islands.note: Conference paper. Corroborates the Smithsonian account of construction method.

establishes: Tom Ecker's Olympic Facts and Fables is held in the IOC's own library, establishing it as a recognised Olympic-history reference
It is the published origin of the challenge to the Owens-Long advice story
ecker-olympic-facts-fables.note: This entry establishes the standing of the challenge, not its truth. The substance of Ecker's account comes from npr-owens-long-myth. The question is written to report the dispute, not resolve it.

establishes: Socotra has 825 vascular plant species in 430 genera; 307 species (37%) and 15 genera are endemic
34 reptile species with 90% endemism; 96 land snail species with 95% endemism
Socotra sits at the intersection of African, Oriental and Palaearctic biogeographic regions

lindahall-panama-french.publisher: Linda Hall Library of Science, Engineering and Technology
establishes: De Lesseps began the French Panama effort in 1881 insisting on a sea-level canal with no locks
The Compagnie Universelle went bankrupt in 1889
Tropical disease, chiefly malaria and yellow fever, destroyed the workforce
An estimated 22,000 people died of disease during the French construction period
About three quarters of the French engineers who arrived with de Lesseps died within three months
Left Vietnam 1911 working as a kitchen hand at sea; worked in the US and Britain before Paris
Petitioned the 1919 Versailles conference as Nguyen Ai Quoc for equal rights in French Indochina, and was ignored
Founding member of the French Communist Party, December 1920
Trained in Moscow; returned to Vietnam in 1941
britannica-ho-chi-minh.note: The Escoffier pastry-chef anecdote was REMOVED from the question: no contemporary evidence supports it. Do not reintroduce.

establishes: Seven prisoners were in the Bastille on 14 July 1789
The crowd came for gunpowder, having taken muskets from the Invalides
Governor de Launay was killed and his head paraded
The seven were four forgers, two men held as insane, and the Comte de Solages, imprisoned at his family's request
29,000-32,000 muskets were taken from the Invalides without powder; 250 barrels of powder had been moved to the Bastille
Louis Meyer drank buttermilk after winning in 1936; a photograph led a dairy executive to formalise the tradition
Since 2006 drivers state a milk preference before the race: whole, 2 percent or skim
Kissing the bricks began at the 1996 Brickyard 400 with Dale Jarrett and crew chief Todd Parrott, not at the Indianapolis 500
ims-kiss-bricks.note: Corrects an earlier version of the question that implied the tradition started at the Indy 500.

establishes: Fittipaldi drank orange juice after winning the 1993 Indianapolis 500 and forfeited a $5,000 American Dairy Association of Indiana prize
He was booed for it
deseret-fittipaldi-1993.note: Corroborated by UPI, 1 June 1993, and Tampa Bay Times, 2 June 1993.

matisse-teriade-quote.publisher: Teriade, 'Constance du Fauvisme', Minotaure, 15 October 1936; trans. Jack Flam, Matisse on Art (1995)
establishes: Matisse: 'I don't paint things. I only paint the difference between things.' Said to Teriade, published Minotaure, 15 October 1936
matisse-teriade-quote.note: The URL is a Wikiquote index page, which is NOT the source. The source is the Minotaure article and Flam's translation, both named above. Replace the URL with a Flam citation or the Minotaure scan when available.
matisse-teriade-quote.replace: URL is a Wikiquote index, not the source. Replace with Flam, Matisse on Art (1995), or a Minotaure scan.

establishes: Robbins proposed the show to Bernstein and Laurents in 1949 as East Side Story: a Jewish girl and an Italian Catholic boy on the Lower East Side at Easter and Passover
The rival gangs in that version were the Jets and the Emeralds
Bernstein wrote the score; Sondheim, aged 25, the lyrics
bernstein-wss-official.note: The claim that West Side Story lost the 1958 Best Musical Tony to The Music Man was REMOVED pending a Tony Awards primary citation.

establishes: A 60-km dyke intruded the Dabbahu segment of the Nubia-Arabia boundary in Afar, Ethiopia, in September 2005
It emplaced roughly 2.5 cubic km of magma and is the largest single magmatic rifting episode recorded
Dyke up to 8 m wide between 2 and 9 km depth; horizontal opening 5-8 m
gji-dabbahu-2005.note: Replaces an unsourced '56-kilometre crack over ten days' figure in the earlier version of the question.

establishes: Anning found the first complete ichthyosaur and plesiosaur specimens at Lyme Regis and sold fossils to support her family
As a woman she could not join the Geological Society of London, which admitted women only in 1904, 57 years after her 1847 death
Gentlemen geologists published her finds without crediting her
The Natural History Museum calls her the greatest fossil hunter ever known

dcceew-gab-2024.publisher: Australian Government, Dept of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
establishes: Great Artesian Basin covers about 1.7 million square kilometres, roughly a fifth of the continent
Recharge occurs in upland areas along the Great Dividing Range and the basin's western and northern margins
Basin pressure has declined measurably; uncapped bores were the main historic loss
dcceew-gab-2024.note: The 'water over a million years old' claim was REMOVED from the question; the report does not support that precision.

establishes: 1937: icing rule adopted. A team not shorthanded that shoots the puck from its own zone across the opposing goal line has the faceoff brought back to its own zone once an opponent touches it
A shorthanded team may ice the puck legally
The 2005-06 NHL rules package introduced stricter icing including the line-change ban, removed the centre red line, and added the shootout
espn-2005-rule-changes.note: Corrects an earlier version of the question that attributed the no-line-change rule to 1937. It dates to 2005-06.
espn-2005-rule-changes.replace: Replace with the NHL records page for the 2005-06 rule package.

establishes: In Athenian democracy nearly all magistrates were chosen by lot, beginning with the archons in 487-486 BC
The Boule of 500 and the law-court juries were also chosen by lot
Officials underwent dokimasia, an examination by the Boule and courts before taking office
At the end of a term they underwent euthyna, an audit of conduct, especially financial
Operation Uranus began 19 November 1942 against the Romanian and Hungarian armies holding the German flanks
The Third and Fourth Romanian armies were in retreat by 20 November and the ring closed within days
britannica-operation-uranus.note: Encirclement strength is reported between 250,000 and 300,000 depending on whether Romanian and Croatian units are counted. The question says 'roughly a quarter of a million' rather than pick a figure.

establishes: The Sixth Army surrendered on 31 January and 2 February 1943
Around 91,000 went into Soviet captivity; only a few thousand survived to return
William wanted to know who held which land, who lived there, its value and the tax due
Domesday Book is the oldest government record held at The National Archives
Seven or eight panels of commissioners each worked a separate group of counties
Commissioners held sworn inquests in local courts putting fixed questions to local men
Each property was assessed three times over to capture change across the Conquest
britannica-domesday.note: An earlier version of the question claimed a second team was sent to verify the first. That is not supported here and was REMOVED; the three-times assessment is the sourced detail.

establishes: Hicks was given egg whites, brandy and strychnine sulphate over the last ten miles and was near-carried across the line
Fred Lorz finished first but was disqualified for riding in a car
32 starters from seven nations; only 14 finished
Hicks was hallucinating at the finish as a result of the brandy, raw eggs and strychnine
The course had a single water station, in heat and dust
Wonder let his Motown contract lapse on turning 21 in 1971 and financed his own recordings
The resulting 21-page contract gave him creative control, a 20 percent royalty and his own publishing
It preceded Music of My Mind, Talking Book, Innervisions and Songs in the Key of Life
npr-stevie-wonder-run.note: An earlier version said he 'returned holding the masters'. Not supported; Motown continued to distribute. REMOVED.

establishes: Motown's house system placed creative decisions with staff writers and producers
Wonder's renegotiation was without precedent at the label
Michelangelo painted the ceiling standing on his own wall-anchored bridge scaffolding, not lying on his back
He worked with assistants rather than alone
Michelangelo rejected the papal architect's scheme and designed a bridge anchored to the walls, about seven feet below the vault
He stood with head tilted back and arms overhead, working into wet plaster section by section
He employed as many as thirteen assistants
The ceiling contains nine central scenes from Genesis
ebsco-sistine-chapel.note: Corrects an earlier version claiming 'minimal assistants', which contradicts the record.

establishes: Antarctic interior receives about 50mm precipitation a year in liquid equivalent; the coastal belt roughly 500mm
250mm a year is the common upper limit for a true desert, so the interior qualifies and the coast does not
The Antarctic interior receives the equivalent of only 50mm rainfall a year, comparable to the Sahara
Kilimanjaro ice cover fell from 12.06 sq km in 1912 to 1.85 sq km in 2007, about 85 percent
Loss ran ~1% a year 1912-1953 and ~2.5% a year 1989-2007; 26% of the ice present in 2000 was gone by 2007
pnas-kilimanjaro-ice.note: The question states a dated range (1912 to 2007) rather than a running total, so it cannot expire. Some later sources report 91%.

establishes: Tenochtitlan was built on an island in Lake Texcoco with causeways, aqueducts and chinampas

britannica-tenochtitlan.note: Published estimates run from ~60,000 (Evans) to 200,000-300,000 (Sanders/Parsons/Santley, Calnek) to 400,000. The question gives the range rather than picking a figure.

establishes: Seville had under 50,000 residents in 1530 and about 90,000 by 1594
Nirvana's Nevermind and Pearl Jam's Ten are each certified 13x platinum in the United States
riaa-ten-nevermind.note: Replaces an unqualified claim that Ten 'outsold Nevermind over time', which is true domestically but false worldwide.

establishes: Three Gorges Dam has an installed capacity of 22,500 MW, the largest of any power station
usgs-three-gorges.note: Live superlative. Corroborated by Guinness World Records. Recheck if a larger plant is commissioned.

establishes: Chinese officials raised the displacement total to 1.4 million people
cbc-three-gorges-displacement.note: Corroborated by CNN and Scientific American. The '1,300 archaeological sites' figure was REMOVED from the question as unverified.

establishes: The reservoir holds roughly 40 billion tonnes of water; shifting that mass lengthened the day by 0.06 microseconds
nasa-three-gorges-rotation.replace: Placeholder URL. Find the specific NASA/GSFC page or Chao's paper before this ships.
nasa-three-gorges-rotation.note: Corrects an earlier version that said 'a few hundred-billionths of a second', which understated the effect by roughly 200x.

establishes: Battle of Adwa, 1 March 1896: Menelik II's force of over 100,000 destroyed an Italian army of about 14,500, half Italian and half askari
Italy signed the Treaty of Addis Ababa on 26 October 1896, abrogating Wichale and recognising Ethiopian sovereignty
britannica-adwa.note: Corrects an earlier version giving the Italian force as 'around 17,000'.

establishes: Vostok 1 lasted 108 minutes

The USSR did not admit the separate landing until 1971
Brown signalled fines mid-performance with a splayed hand meaning five dollars, each pulse another five

The African Humid Period ran roughly 11,000 to 5,000 years ago with the Sahara vegetated and lake-covered

nature-green-sahara.note: Corrects an earlier version giving the cycle as 'roughly every 20,000 years'. Also: the swimming-figures rock art is at Wadi Sura in Egypt, not Tassili n'Ajjer; that detail was REMOVED.

establishes: North African humid periods recur over the past 800,000 years, driven by orbital precession
The most recent peaked between about 9,000 and 6,000 years ago
Guardians of the Galaxy grossed $773 million worldwide on a $170 million budget
$333m domestic, $344.5m foreign, $96.5m China

The song runs 5:55; EMI objected to the length
Kenny Everett played it on Capital Radio fourteen times in two days before release, from a reel-to-reel
The operatic section took close to a month, with Roy Baker splicing in tape as Mercury kept adding Galileos
udiscover-bohemian-rhapsody.note: Corrects an earlier version giving the opera section as 'roughly three weeks'. The 'tape worn thin enough to see through' anecdote was REMOVED as unverifiable.

establishes: Orban, a Hungarian founder, first offered his services to the defenders before casting bombards for Mehmed II
The largest bombard was about 27 feet (8m) long with a 30-inch bore
It fired stone balls of roughly 600 to 680 kg
Reload took hours; the Theodosian Walls could not be repaired fast enough
historynet-guns-constantinople.note: Corrects an earlier version giving the shot as 'half a tonne'; the sourced range is above that.

establishes: Woods finished 18 under, 270, a tournament record until Dustin Johnson beat it in 2020
He won by twelve strokes over Tom Kite, the largest margin in Masters history
At 21 he was the youngest and first non-white Masters winner
Augusta did not invite a Black player until Lee Elder in 1975, the year Woods was born
pgatour-1997-masters.note: The '1990 first Black member' and '1983 caddie rule' details were REMOVED as unverified in this pass. The Lee Elder fact carries the same point and is sourced.

establishes: Get Out grossed over $255 million on a $4.5 million budget and was the most profitable film of 2017
Peele was the first African American to win the Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay
He was the first African American nominated for producing, writing and directing in the same year

lithub-milch-obscenity.publisher: Literary Hub (David Milch, in his own words)
establishes: Milch's research found mining-camp speech was of unrelieved coarseness
Period profanity was blasphemous rather than scatological, so he substituted modern obscenity to carry the same force
Milch designed the camp as a society inventing law without outside governance
HBO cancelled Deadwood after season three; a 2019 film concluded the story
Vent communities found February 1977 at the Galapagos Rift from RV Knorr using the ANGUS camera sled

Colleen Cavanaugh proposed the chemosynthetic symbiosis mechanism in 1981
whoi-vent-discovery-1977.note: An earlier version implied chemosynthesis was understood in 1977. The mechanism came in 1981; the question now separates the two.

establishes: The Po Valley is the most polluted region in Western Europe and regularly exceeds annual PM limits
eea-po-valley.replace: Link the specific EEA air-quality report page for the Po Valley rather than the topic index.

establishes: The Alps to the north and Apennines to the south enclose the valley; winter temperature inversions trap emissions rather than dispersing them

plutarch-alexander-iliad.publisher: Plutarch, Life of Alexander (Loeb, via UChicago)
establishes: Plutarch, citing Onesicritus, reports Alexander kept Aristotle's corrected Iliad, the 'casket copy', with a dagger under his pillow
He called it a portable treasury of military virtue
plutarch-alexander-iliad.note: A single ancient report, not an independently documented fact. The question option was changed from 'annotated by Aristotle himself' to 'said to be Aristotle's own' and the explanation now attributes it to Plutarch and Onesicritus.

ahf-target-committee.publisher: Atomic Heritage Foundation / National Museum of Nuclear Science and History
establishes: A 15 May 1945 directive reserved Hiroshima, Kyoto and Niigata from conventional firebombing so the atomic effect could be assessed on undamaged cities
Kokura was added to the reserved list on 27 June
Stimson had Kyoto removed on cultural and religious grounds; Nagasaki replaced it in late July
ahf-target-committee.note: The 'Stimson honeymooned in Kyoto' anecdote was REMOVED. Historian Alex Wellerstein argues at nuclearsecrecy.com that it is a misconception. The cultural-significance grounds are not disputed. Specific casualty figures were also removed; published ranges vary too widely to state one.

establishes: Bockscar circled Kokura three times on 9 August without clear visibility
A break in cloud over Nagasaki let bombardier Kermit Beahan sight the city, and he was authorised to bomb either
Humans were too difficult to animate convincingly in 1995, which is why Pixar centred the film on toys

About 800,000 machine hours for the film's 114,200 frames
Hotel California first hit number one on the Billboard 200 dated 15 January 1977
It spent eight non-consecutive weeks at number one across four separate stints
billboard-hotel-california.note: Corrects an earlier version implying eight consecutive weeks.

establishes: Wood consistently rejected suggestions that American Gothic satirised the Midwest and its conservative values
He intended a positive image of rural American values, reassurance at the start of the Depression
The models were his dentist B.H. McKeeby and his sister Nan, posed as farmer and daughter
Inspired by a Carpenter Gothic house at Eldon, Iowa
Debuted at the Art Institute in 1930, winning Wood a $300 prize
artic-american-gothic.note: CRITICAL CORRECTION. The earlier version of this question asserted Wood intended 'a gentle satire of small-town Midwestern puritanism'. That is the popular reading and the opposite of what he said. The question was rewritten to ask what Wood said about the satire reading.

establishes: Pakistan's transfer was 14 August 1947 in Karachi and India's at midnight into 15 August in Delhi
Between 12 and 20 million people crossed the new borders
britannica-partition.note: Corrects an earlier '10 to 20 million' figure.

establishes: Cyril Radcliffe had never visited India and drew the boundary in about five weeks

Mountbatten attended the Karachi ceremony on the 14th then flew to Delhi
Partial skull and tibia of a 14-year-old English girl, 'Jane', from a 1609-10 trash deposit show cut marks consistent with survival cannibalism
First scientifically proven case of survival cannibalism in colonial America
About 500 people were in James Fort at the start of winter 1609-10; roughly 61 were alive by spring
A Powhatan siege cut the fort off from relief alongside disease and shortage
smithsonian-jamestown-cannibalism.note: Corrects an earlier version giving 'roughly 300 colonists, around 60 survived'.

establishes: Phelps touched in 50.58 to Cavic's 50.59 in the Beijing 100m butterfly

Brian Cullinan and Martha Ruiz were permanently removed from all Academy work

Alternative explanations: the 'dogs' may have been monk seals, or the name may come from the Canarii Berber people
